# A workflow's paths: allowlist is credited as a mirror without checking it covers the guard's scan surface

## Context

`check-guard-ci-parity.mjs` (relocated here by PR #18753 for #17783) requires every `lint-staged` guard to be mirrored by a workflow gating `dev` PRs. It deliberately credits a workflow carrying a `paths:` allowlist, and says why in its own source at [`buildScripts/util/check-guard-ci-parity.mjs:259-264`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/buildScripts/util/check-guard-ci-parity.mjs#L259-L264):

> *"A `paths` ALLOWLIST is deliberately not rejected here, where `paths-ignore` is. […] The allowlist is conditional, so eligibility for it is not free; it is an alignment question, **and until that predicate exists** an allowlist is credited rather than reported as eight false defects."*

This ticket is that predicate. @neo-opus-ada released this half to me on 2026-09-15 ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17171#issuecomment-5686964171)) with the identity that makes it one lane: *"`scan ⊆ paths` and 'scanned ⊆ watched' are the same predicate under two names"*.

Live latest-open sweep 2026-09-16T12:40Z — latest 20 open issues plus a targeted `paths scan surface workflow filter covering mirror` search: only #18754 (the single-guard instance; PR #18790 open). A2A sweep over the latest 30 messages: no competing `[lane-claim]`. Raw-memory sweep on the same terms: no prior art.

## The Problem

A mirror whose filter does not cover what its guard reads is a **false green**: the workflow exists, the parity guard credits it, and an edit in the uncovered region never re-runs it. `git commit --no-verify` then ships past both layers with nothing downstream — the exact hole `check-guard-ci-parity` exists to close, one level in.

The predicate does not exist because it has nothing to read. Measured on `dev` today — the partition is the parity guard's own, not a hand census (`[lint-guard-ci-parity] OK (15 lint-staged guards, 5 accepted client-only)`):

| | |
|---|---|
| guards invoked by `lint-staged` | **15** |
| …accepted `clientOnly`: no mirror, so no alignment question | **5** |
| **mirrored — the population this ticket governs** | **10** |
| …that expose a scan surface to an importer | **5**, under 2 names (`SCAN_SURFACE` ×4, `DEFAULT_SCAN_PATHS` ×1) |
| …that know their scan surface but keep it module-private | **5** — `check-jsdoc-types#DEFAULT_DIRS`, `check-relative-links#SCAN_ROOTS`, `check-theme-value-files#themeRoot`, `check-theme-coverage`'s three dirs, `check-content-logical-identity#archiveRoot` |

So the shape is better than "nine guards cannot answer": **every mirrored guard already knows what it reads.** Five state it where a spec can ask and five state it where only a reader can, and the two that state it publicly disagree about what to call it. The predicate is unwritable for a naming reason, not a knowledge one — which is why it can be closed in one PR rather than ten.

**One live true positive**, found by reading the six declarations by hand:

`check-jsdoc-types.mjs:37` scans `['src', 'ai', 'examples', 'apps', 'docs/app']`, and says so in its own success line — *"1233 file(s) read, 0 unparseable type expressions (docs-build parse scope: src, ai, examples, apps, docs/app)"*. `jsdoc-type-lint.yml`'s `paths:` carries four of those five. `ai` is absent — and must be: `git ls-files ai` → **0**.

Same pre-split residue as #18754, one guard over, and it fails more quietly: `collectDefaultFiles` tolerates `find`'s non-zero exit by design, so nothing errors. The guard simply reports a scope it does not have.

## The Architectural Reality

The predicate is **not** `scan ⊆ paths`. An untracked member is unreachable by any `paths:` filter, so a raw subset test reports a defect no workflow edit can fix — and #18754 settles that direction: such a member does not belong in a scan surface at all. Two clauses, not one:

- **`tracked(member) ≠ ∅`** for every declared member — the #18754 invariant, generalized from one guard to the population.
- **`scan ∩ tracked ⊆ paths`** — every tracked file a guard reads is reachable by its mirror's filter.

The first makes the second's `∩ tracked` a check rather than a silent narrowing. Without it, dropping a root into a gitignored directory would *satisfy* alignment by shrinking the left side.

The denominator is the third clause and the one that keeps this honest. `check-guard-ci-parity` already supplies it: its `clientOnly` registry partitions the 15 into 5 accepted-unmirrored and 10 mirrored, so the population is *derived* rather than authored here, and a guard that gains a mirror joins this predicate's scope in the same edit. Within those ten, an undeclared surface is a defect — not an unknown, and not a new registry row, because all ten already know their surface.

## The Fix

1. One export name across the ten. `SCAN_SURFACE` is already the plurality (4 of 5 public); `check-ticket-archaeology#DEFAULT_SCAN_PATHS` renames onto it and the five private declarations become exports. Members are globs, because `paths:` filters are globs and comparing a bare root against one is where a hand-rolled subset test produces a confident wrong answer.
2. Drop `ai` from `check-jsdoc-types`, with the rule at the export site — the #18754 remedy, applied to the instance this ticket found.
3. The predicate as a spec beside the existing `buildScripts` unit arms, asserting all three clauses over the population **derived** from `lint-staged` minus the registry's `clientOnly` rows — never a hardcoded list, for the reason `discoverGuards()` already gives.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guard scan-surface declaration | Each mirrored `buildScripts/util/check-*.mjs` — `lint-staged` population minus the registry's `clientOnly` rows | Exports `SCAN_SURFACE` as globs | none: within the ten there is no accepted-undeclared state, because all ten already know their surface | export-site JSDoc naming the tracked-member rule | the spec's denominator arm: every derived mirrored guard exports one |
| Mirror filter alignment | `check-guard-ci-parity`'s eligible-workflow set | A credited `paths:` allowlist must cover the guard's tracked scan surface | none — an uncovered tracked path is a defect claim, not an unknown | the `:259` comment is replaced by the predicate it defers to | seeded-drift red control: narrowing one workflow's `paths:` reds the spec |
| `check-jsdoc-types` scope | `DEFAULT_DIRS` → `SCAN_SURFACE` | `ai` dropped; the reported scope equals the scope read | none | export-site rule, as #18754 | `git ls-files ai` → 0; the success line stops naming a root it cannot read |

Retirement: folds into `neo-agent-skills#14`'s unified governance when its reusable workflow supersedes per-repo callers — the same retirement #17783 names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: a spec asserts, over the population **derived** from `lint-staged`, that every declared scan-surface member is tracked (`git ls-files <member>` non-empty).
- [ ] AC-2: a spec asserts `scan ∩ tracked ⊆ paths` for every guard that declares a surface AND is credited by `check-guard-ci-parity` through a `paths:` allowlist.
- [ ] AC-3: red control — narrowing one mirror's `paths:` below its guard's declared surface reds AC-2's arm; the narrowing is reverted in the same run.
- [ ] AC-4: the denominator is asserted — every mirrored guard (derived: `lint-staged` minus `clientOnly`) exports `SCAN_SURFACE`. A guard that does not fails, and a guard leaving `clientOnly` joins the population without anyone editing a list.
- [ ] AC-5: `check-jsdoc-types` no longer claims `ai`, and its reported scope equals what it reads.
- [ ] AC-6: `check-guard-ci-parity.mjs:259`'s comment no longer defers to a predicate that does not exist.
- [ ] AC-7: `npx playwright test --config playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/buildScripts` green, and every touched guard's CLI behavior unchanged — each declaration is a rename or an export, never a change to what the guard reads. The single exception is AC-5, which is the point.

**Not claimed by this ticket:** alignment for the five `clientOnly` guards. They have no mirror, so there is no filter to align; when one gains a mirror it enters this predicate's population automatically, which is why the population is derived rather than listed.

## Out of Scope

- The required-status-context decision (#17171, operator-owned) — this is the coverage half, not the enforcement half.
- Changing what any guard checks, or its CLI surface.
- Workflows that gate `dev` but run no `lint-staged` guard (`class-hierarchy-freshness`, `file-size-guard`, `consumer-runtime-build`, `check-package-contents`, `check-examples-body-only`, `check-theme-surfaces`): outside `check-guard-ci-parity`'s stated population, and pulling them in is a second ticket with its own authority question.
- `neo-agent-brain`'s `lintWorkflowScanRootParity.spec.mjs` — the Brain-side twin, which governs `ai/scripts/lint/**` and names no `buildScripts/util/` guard.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not write `scan ⊆ paths`.** It reports eight defects no workflow edit can fix, which is exactly the false-defect family `check-guard-ci-parity:259` refused to create. The tracked intersection is the whole difficulty.
- ⛔ **Do not let the predicate cover only the guards that already declare.** A gate whose denominator is its own numerator is green by construction. AC-4 is not optional polish; it is what makes AC-2 mean anything.
- ⛔ **Do not hardcode the guard list.** `discoverGuards()` already states why: a hardcoded list answers today's question and rots, and a renamed guard leaves the population silently.
- ⛔ **Do not compare a root to a glob by string prefix.** `src` and `src/**/*.mjs` are the same surface; `test/playwright` and `test/playwright/unit/**` are not. This is where a hand-rolled subset test produces a confident wrong answer.
- ⛔ **Do not start before PR #18790 merges.** It changes `check-ticket-archaeology`'s declaration and its spec; rebasing a rename onto it is avoidable churn.

- 2026-09-16T13:44:30Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `5268f75` - "feat(buildScripts): a mirror's paths filter is held to what its guard reads (#18791)

check-guard-ci-parity answers whether a guard is mirrored at all, and deliberately
credits a workflow carrying a `paths:` allowlist without inspecting it. Its source
said why, and deferred: "it is an alignment question, and until that predicate
exists an allowlist is credited". This is that predicate.

A filter narrower than the surface it credits is a false green of the exact class
that lint exists to catch, one layer in: the workflow exists, the guard counts as
mirrored, and an edit in the uncovered region never re-runs it. `--no-verify` then
passes both layers.

The predicate could not be written because it had nothing to read. Of the ten
mirrored guards, five exposed a scan surface (under two names) and five kept it
module-private. All ten knew what they read; the blocker was naming, not knowledge,
which is why it closes in one change rather than ten.

`scan subset of paths` would be the wrong predicate. An untracked member is
unreachable by any filter, so the raw subset test manufactures defects no workflow
edit can fix -- the false-defect family the deferral refused to create. Three
clauses instead: every declared member is tracked (#18754's invariant, generalized
from one guard to the population), every tracked file of a surface is selected by
some mirror, and the denominator -- every mirrored guard declares -- because a gate
whose denominator is its own numerator is green by construction. The population is
derived from lint-staged minus the registry's clientOnly rows, so a guard that gains
a mirror enters the arms in the same edit.

The filter is evaluated as GitHub evaluates it: each mirror separately, its patterns
in order, a leading `!` excluding, the last match deciding, and a file no pattern
matches not selected at all. An unordered "does any pattern match" test over a
flattened list of every mirror's patterns credits `['src/**', '!src/**']`, which
selects nothing -- reproducing this defect inside the check for it. That is what the
first draft did, and @neo-opus-grace's review caught it with four filters that a
workflow could plausibly carry.

check-jsdoc-types was the live true positive: it scanned `ai` and said so in its
success line, while `git ls-files ai` is 0 and its mirror's filter could not name
it. Same pre-split residue as #18754, one guard over, and quieter -- the guard
tolerates find's non-zero exit, so it reported a scope it did not have with nothing
to show for it. File count is identical either way (1233), which is the measure of
what the claim was worth.

The archive guard's quoted refusal now shows its shape rather than one pull
request's number: the published archaeology guard reads that number as a tracking
ref while the repo-local copy does not, so the hook passed and CI failed. The
published verdict is the one that gates, and it is right -- a specific number in a
durable comment is the decay the guard exists to prevent.

Also folds @neo-opus-ada's non-blocking finding from the #18790 review: the
absent-root arm's `not.toContain('src,')` could not fail for the reason its message
gave, so it read as a witness it was not."
